findings.problem: The CPU parser keeps only aggregate total and idle. A user counter falling 100→90 while system rises 50→70 and idle rises 850→930 yields a valid-looking 0.1111 busy sample. Individual counter reset/regression is not rejected.
findings.impact: Malformed/reset kernel counters can become a healthy readiness observation and understate CPU pressure.
findings.independent_reproduction: Twice replayed mocked /proc/stat values through sampleLinuxHost; both returned cpuBusyFraction 0.1111111111111111 without refusal.

findings.problem: linuxProcessGroupMembers ignores EACCES when reading a candidate /proc/<pid>/stat; an unreadable live member is treated as absent. stopLinuxOwnedGroup can then return true after SIGTERM without proving the group gone.
findings.impact: A cleanup failure can be reported as success, allowing eventual lease release or admission over live owned work if wired into the guard.
findings.independent_reproduction: Twice injected EACCES for a still-live group leader after the initial owner check; linuxProcessGroupMembers returned [], and stopLinuxOwnedGroup returned true.

findings.problem: The stop primitive requires the root PID to remain present at cleanup start. If the leader exited while a child remains in its process group, it refuses to stop that child; inherited-token descendant scanning and stale-owner recovery are not implemented.
findings.impact: The unit does not yet prove terminal or stale cleanup of all owned Linux processes.
findings.independent_reproduction: Injected census containing only surviving child PID 102 in group 101; stopLinuxOwnedGroup threw RESOURCE_MEASUREMENT_INVALID:linux-process-owner without sending a stop signal.

verdict_B_safety_quality.test_assessment: The new synthetic tests validate one healthy and one stalled PSI fixture and a live leader stop on Ubuntu, but omit the above failure mutations. Passing nine tests on macOS gives no Linux execution evidence. No test assertions were promoted to product pass.
